speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The copper is on. You will stand out of the steam.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Galls, copperas, and gum. That is the receipt. I have not changed it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I should hope not. I boil it on Mondays from your receipt, and I will not be taught a new gall in Lent.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The galls are the oak-galls from the jar, Mistress. I did not buy more. The copperas is the same paper, and the gum.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Twopence the horn, and he had a new one on Saturday. This boil is the house's, until that horn is dry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not want another before Lady Day. Twopence is enough horn for the fast.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It smells of the oak when it takes. The cat has left the kitchen.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Gib has more sense than a man who leans over a copper. Back, Master Shakespeare.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am only looking whether the gum has gone in. Left dry on the board, it is a stone by morning.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: It has gone in. Alse stirred it. You may trust a girl who does not write in it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I stirred to a hundred, as you said. I did not lose the count.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A hundred is the receipt. Thank you, Alse.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You will have quiet after nine whether the ink settles or not. I am not running a tiring-house.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No one on the floor who is not of the house. No candle nearer the copper than the hearth.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And no supper counted twice. If you board, it is threepence, and you do not board every night. Two or three times in a week is the bargain.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know the bargain.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is salt herring, if you are down. I have set it back from the steam.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: He can smell his own dinner. Let the ink alone.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Monday's ink, then. The horn on the desk stays the one I paid for.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Twopence, Saturday. I have it in the housekeeping. Do not pay it again and call me careless.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not pay it twice.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I take a horn up when this is cool, or leave it?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it. The horn upstairs is full enough. The letter it was for is already written.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then the copper is my business. Go and be a lodger.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is the right smell. I will know it if anyone improves it.
